ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-aligned screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against: (i) United Nations Security Council sanctions implemented under the United Nations Act and Canadian sanctions regulations adopted under the Special Economic Measures Act; (ii) FINTRAC published risk notices and guidance for Money Service Businesses and digital payments; (iii) OSFI compliance expectations for financial-sector counterparties; (iv) OFAC SDN, consolidated sanctions, and sectoral sanctions lists as the de facto standard required by Apple IAP and Google Play Billing processors and US-domiciled payment intermediaries; (v) domestic federal and provincial politically exposed person (PEP) data sets; enhanced due diligence (EDD) and source-of-funds verification are mandatory for PEPs, for Medium_Risk_Enhanced social-casino publishing activity, and for any non-resident UBO controlling 25% or more of the entity; re-screening is triggered at onboarding, upon any ownership or officer change, upon sanctions-list updates, and at annual renewal of the AML compliance program.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (NUANS Pre-Screen and Name Reservation accessible via ised-isde.canada.ca and corporations-canada.ic.gc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: CBCA s. 10 and Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512: a corporate name must comprise Roman letters, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation only; non-Roman scripts (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, etc.) are not accepted in the registered legal name; any foreign-language/foreign-script trade name must be transliterated into English or French and the transliterated form must pass the NUANS proximity test; the standard federal name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element (Inc., Corp., Ltd., or Ltée); bilingual names may be combined (e.g., X Development Inc. / X Développement Inc.) and each linguistic version is governed by the same confusion standard.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada (as a leading or sole distinctive element without ministerial authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No automatic statutory extension exists for a federal name reservation; after 90 days the NUANS report lapses and a new search and reservation filing (with new fees) is required. Upon name rejection by Corporations Canada, counsel may: (i) revise the distinctive element and re-file a fresh NUANS search; (ii) submit a Director-level re-examination request citing distinguishing factors and supporting common-law or trademark evidence; (iii) where a third party objects on confusion grounds, the objector may bring an application under CBCA s. 12 within 90 days of the name's adoption and the Director may order a change of name; (iv) after exhaustion of administrative remedies, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Federal Court pursuant to the Federal Courts Act, with an application filed within 30 days of the final refusal decision; no separate Corporation Canada appeal fee is charged, but professional fees and re-filing NUANS costs apply at each stage.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with substantive guardrails: CBCA s. 19 requires a registered office in a province specified in the articles, located at a physical street address accessible for service of process during normal business hours; a licensed virtual-office provider supplying a physical address, mail forwarding, and registered-agent services is generally accepted; however, for a social-casino publisher using Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, platform developer-account reviews, licensed payment processors, and FINTRAC AML obligations may require demonstrable Canadian commercial substance including operational records, corporate records location, and an agent physically able to receive regulators; a mere post office box or a non-Canadian address will not satisfy the statute.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate for this industry class: quantified probability of an unannounced on-site compliance inspection is estimated at 20–35% within the first 24 months of operation, reflecting the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier for simulated gambling/social-casino publishing; risk rises to approximately 40% if the entity triggers CRA business-verification site visits, FINTRAC AML program audits, or manual developer-account/payment-processor substance checks for non-resident UBOs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended; ss. 4-19 (Incorporation), ss. 101-126 (Directors and Officers), ss. 128-134 (Records and Reporting), ss. 210-214 (Fundamental Changes).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, a special operating agency of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 3) filed through the online Corporations Canada filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a Business Corporation incorporated under the CBCA. Shares may be issued with or without par value. No escrow or capitalization deposit is required at incorporation; initial capitalization may be nominal and funded via share subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the board of directors (i) accepts the subscriptions for common shares in the capital of the Corporation as recorded in the Share Subscription and Allotment Register; (ii) adopts the registered office at the address set out in the Articles of Incorporation; (iii) appoints the officers listed in the Officer Appointment Schedule with authority to execute banking, licensing, and commercial agreements; (iv) approves the issuance of share certificates and the maintenance of corporate registers; and (v) authorizes management to file all necessary regulatory and tax registration documents. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online name search system and NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name query through the Corporations Canada 'Name Search' tool or a licensed NUANS provider. Review the preliminary name availability and obtain an official NUANS report to reserve the name. The name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing trademarks or corporate names. If using a number name, skip this step.
required_dossiers: NUANS search request and report fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name application with a new NUANS report or apply for an objection hearing within 30 days. The incorporation documents may be resubmitted with a corrected name without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles of Incorporation and Registered Office Address
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada filing portal (online) or mail to Corporations Canada headquarters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 3 - Articles of Incorporation, setting out the corporate name or numbered name, share structure, restrictions (if any), statement of registered office, number of directors and any special rights attached to share classes. This step must identify the initial registered office address; the address must be a physical address in Canada where records will be kept.
required_dossiers: Initial registered office address and mailing address
Statement of share classes and director count
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corporations Canada will issue a defect notice; the applicant may correct the filed document and refile electronically within the stated response period, typically 10 business days, without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Corporations Canada online filing system and submit Form 3 along with the prescribed filing fee ($200 CAD online). Review all data entries for accuracy. Payment and submission are instantaneous; the system generates an acknowledgment with a file number. The application is automatically processed and a Certificate of Incorporation is issued when all statutory requirements are met.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing fails because of an incomplete data field, the system provides a validation list. Correct the fields and resubmit. If the application is rejected on substance, request reconsideration or file amended articles within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Obtain Incorporation Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful processing, download the Certificate of Incorporation and the electronic copy of the Articles of Incorporation. The corporation is now a legal entity under the CBCA. Retain the certificate for bank account opening and government registrations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by Corporations Canada)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate cannot be issued due to missing documents, Corporations Canada requests the missing item and provides a 30-day curing period. If no cure is made, the application is terminated with refund of the fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Initial Organizational By-laws and Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting in person or by resolution in writing. Adopt the by-laws governing share transfers, meetings, officers, banking resolution, execution of documents, and fiscal year end. Appoint the initial directors and officers. Record all resolutions in the corporate minute book. Complete share certificates and register share subscriptions.
required_dossiers: Organizational board resolution (written or meeting minutes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is invalid due to lack of quorum or defective notice, the directors may convene a corrective meeting or sign a unanimous written resolution. The minute book should be updated accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Federal Business Number and Tax Accounts with the CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration online service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN). Simultaneously open the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (if revenue exceeds $30,000 or voluntarily), and payroll account if employees are anticipated. This can be done online using the incorporation file number.
required_dossiers: Directors' names and social insurance numbers (or incorporation number for online registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the application, respond to the request for information within the deadline stated in the notice. The BN is typically issued immediately online; if mail application is used, allow 10 to 15 business days and follow up at the CRA Business Number hotline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Corporate Records and Share Allotment Documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary / Registered Agent and Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and maintain the corporate minute book containing the articles, by-laws, board minutes, share ledger, certificates, register of directors, register of officers, and registered office register. Issue fully paid share certificates to the initial subscribers as per the board resolution and record transfers in the securities register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Missing registers can be recreated and certified by the corporate secretary. If records are lost, complete a notarized affidavit and re-execute replacement documents under board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Provincial Extra-Provincial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or financial institution and applicable provincial Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business bank account in the corporate name using the Certificate of Incorporation, the corporate minute book, and the banking resolution with the designated signing officers. If the corporation carries on business outside its registered office province, file an extra-provincial registration with that province's corporate registry without delay.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Banks may require updated CRA screenshots or a proof of address; provide CRA Form RC145. If provincial registration is rejected, correct the corporate status by paying arrears or filing a name change and refile.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – no physical industrial establishment or manufacturing facility is required for software publishing under ISIC 5820. Where an office lease exists, local municipal business licensing may apply, administered by the municipal licensing department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory gaming or industrial operating license is required for social casino software publishing; operations are conducted under the general CBCA corporate registration and applicable provincial consumer protection and IP laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / applicable provincial environmental ministry
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Full EIA not required. Office-based software publishing generates negligible physical emissions and does not meet thresholds listed under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012 (Impact Assessment Act). Provincial permitting obligations, if any, are limited to general municipal commercial occupancy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – zero industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. Compliance with local building sanitation and recycling bylaws is sufficient. If a server data centre is used, the provider must maintain relevant energy and environmental standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The leased office premises must obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire marshal, ensure compliance with the National Fire Code, and undergo structural load verification for office occupancy. Provincial occupational health and safety clearance is required via the applicable labour authority before employees occupy the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; primary portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business/business-registration-online.html). Federal corporate income tax is reported on the T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; GST/HST is reported on the GST/HST return (GST34/GST 400).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a federal Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act via Corporations Canada (name search through the NUANS system, filing of articles of incorporation, receipt of the corporation number). Step 2: Obtain the CRA Business Number (BN) automatically upon incorporation through the CRA and Corporations Canada integration, or file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) through Business Registration Online; the BN is the 9-digit federal tax identifier with a two-letter program account suffix (RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, RZ for import/export, RP for payroll). Step 3: Register the RT program account prior to making taxable supplies in Canada; non-resident digital-economy suppliers may use CRA's simplified GST/HST registration for non-resident persons, which requires only legal name, foreign address, entity type, foreign tax registration number and an authorized representative holding a CRA RepID. Step 4: Enrol the RC program account for T2 filings and activate My Business Account using the access code issued by CRA. Step 5: Where the corporation has non-resident shareholders or connected non-resident platform operators, prepare transfer-pricing documentation (Form RC1410) and file Form T106 if reportable non-arm's length transactions exist. Step 6: Open RP (payroll) and RZ (customs) accounts only if employees or physical merchandise are introduced; a pure digital social-casino publishing model generally requires only RC and RT program accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: A federal Business Corporation is deemed resident in Canada under Income Tax Act subsection 250(4)(a) and is taxed at the entity level under Part I of the Income Tax Act; no pass-through eligibility exists for a corporation. The federal general corporate rate is 15% (38% statutory rate less 10% provincial abatement less 13% general rate reduction); a Canadian-controlled private corporation may access the 9% small business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income. A resident corporation is taxed on worldwide income while a non-resident-owned corporation carrying on business through a Canadian permanent establishment is taxed only on Canadian-source income. Foreign revenue from the digital gaming business is included in Canadian taxable income with a foreign tax credit available under section 126 of the Income Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box entity classification election. Available elections: (i) subsection 89(11) election among associated corporations to allocate the small business limit; (ii) section 216 election permitting a non-resident to file a return and pay tax on Canadian rental or timber income; (iii) subsection 115.2 election for a non-resident corporation to file a simplified Canadian income tax return under an income tax treaty; (iv) subsection 128.1(4) election for a corporation migrating from Canada on a deemed disposition basis; (v) for GST/HST purposes, the simplified non-resident digital-service supplier registration election under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act and the closely-related corporation election under section 156 (intercorporate supplies at nil consideration); (vi) hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.4 through 18.6 of the Income Tax Act are mandatory recharacterization provisions that operate without taxpayer election and do not create a Canadian analogue to an entity classification check-the-box regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (the central bank) retains monetary policy authority; foreign exchange oversight is distributed via the Department of Finance Canada, while the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers anti-money laundering and commercial transaction reporting. Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign exchange control administration; the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act govern the national monetary framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under both current account and capital account in the IMF Articles of Agreement sense. Canada imposes no exchange controls restricting convertibility, dividend repatriation, interest payments, licence royalties, or capital disinvestment. Corporate profits may be remitted abroad without prior regulatory approval, subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (typically 25% under domestic law, reducible by tax treaty) and the general compliance requirements of the Income Tax Act. The Investment Canada Act may apply as a review mechanism for non-resident control of Canadian businesses, but this is not a currency control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory export proceeds surrender rule. Exporters and service providers, including software and social-casino license suppliers, are not required to convert foreign currency receipts into CAD within any prescribed timeline, nor are they required to remit export proceeds to any designated account. All foreign currency earnings may be retained, held in foreign-denominated accounts, or deployed as treasury policy dictates, provided FINTRAC reporting thresholds (including large transaction reports and cross-border currency reporting) are satisfied.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with probative legal constraints. Non-Canadian fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) may operate for Canadian corporate clients only if the provider is properly registered with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business (MSB), which is required for foreign money services businesses directing services at Canada. Alternatively, a fintech may obtain an E-Money Institution licence from another jurisdiction, but that licence does not replace Canadian MSB registration. Funds held with unregulated foreign EMIs are not covered by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC); if the EMI is not an MSB, opening and funding the account creates reverse money laundering and counterparty sanctions exposure. For social-casino distribution, the acceptance of USD payouts via payment facilitators such as Stripe, Adyen, or digital bank accounts may be allowed, provided the EMI has a compliant anti-money laundering (AML) program that treats the mobile gaming revenue as a consumer digital-payments flow. Legally prudent architects will use an EMI only as a secondary collection rail, not as a primary repository of shareholder capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch visit is not a statutory precondition for opening a corporate bank account in Canada. Federal and provincial Business Corporations Act entities may open accounts on a fully remote basis if an online KYC process permits identity verification via a notarized director attestation, video call, or a regulated digital identity platform. However, banks with internal enhanced-due-diligence structures commonly require an in-person or video interview for at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner, especially where the corporation is wholly owned by non-residents or engaged in higher-risk digital activities such as social-casino monetisation. In practice, a remote account opening is achievable but only where the corporate packet is exhaustive, the UBO declaration is complete, and the interviewer confirms that the commercial operations do not constitute 'real-money gambling' under the Criminal Code. A physical in-country presence remains advisable when opening treasury accounts for capital escrow or large cross-border inflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate business description and website display simulated slot machines or casino-style mechanics, triggering a suspicion that the entity engages in real-money gambling or illegal gaming under the Criminal Code.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal legal opinion from a licensed Canadian lawyer confirming the product uses no real-money stakes, no cash-out functionality, no 'house-banked' wagering redemption, and qualifies as a social-casino application exempt from the Criminal Code's gaming provisions; the current certificate of incumbency; a detailed product and payment-flow diagram showing in-app purchases are exclusively for virtual credit; independent expert certification of the virtual items terms and conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High non-resident ownership concentration or shareholder jurisdiction exposed to sanctions, tax evasion, or unexplained wealth, triggering enhanced due diligence and favorable-source verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Register with each ultimate beneficial owner's government-issued identity documentation; certified passport and proof of residence; a bank reference from the shareholder's home-country bank; a summary of the shareholders' wealth profile and source of funds for capital subscription; signed declarations confirming no affiliation with sanctioned persons or entities; in the case of legal-entity shareholders, the entire chain until an individual is disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of app-store payment rails (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) with payment transactions having high volume, many small deposits and no corresponding real-currency withdrawals, which can appear like layering or suspicious structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The application's full payments architecture showing that all end-user purchases are routed through Apple or Google who act as officially recognized merchant-of-record; audited monthly payment settlement reports from the app stores; a list of chargeback and refund policies; a transaction monitoring policy that flags abnormal purchase velocity; a certified AML program incorporating FINTRAC obligations, designated-person screening, and ongoing transaction surveillance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unconfigured treasury and intercompany cross-border wires from a Canadian parent to a non-resident subsidiary or service provider where the stated purpose code is not aligned with the actual service, triggering Financial Intelligence Unit reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany agreements (development, licensing, support) with a transfer-pricing memo compliant with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; specifically completed cross-border wire instruction sheets containing correct SWIFT fields, purpose codes, and beneficiary identifiers; invoices matching the exact remittance rationale; board resolutions approving recurring disbursement limits; and a documented escalation path to the compliance officer for any future change in settlement counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be routed through the Canadian banking system with a compliant wire transfer protocol. A standard SWIFT MT103/MT202 from a foreign bank to the Canadian bank is customary; the remitter must include in field 70 the precise corporate-purpose description, e.g., 'Capital contribution for issued shares' or 'Paid-in capital under Business Corporations Act'; field 57 must contain the beneficiary bank's BIC (e.g., ROYCCAT2 or TDOMCATTTOR), and the beneficiary account should be a CAD current account or an escrow account legally identified as a capital-escrow deposit. Supporting documentation retained by the Canadian receiving bank generally includes a board resolution approving the subscription of shares, a share-subscription agreement, the National Instrument 45-106 accredited investor exemption filing for private placements (if applicable), and the capital call notice from the corporation. FinCEN/FINTRAC exchange-of-information requirements may trigger a large-value transaction report for CAD $10,000 or more, but no prior central-bank foreign-exchange approval is required. For Company Act statutory capital filings, amounts must be reconciled with the article-of-continuance share capital and the minute-book issuance ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operational disbursements for ISIC 5820 software and social-casino publishing utilize three primary clearing rails in Canada: (a) domestic CAD clearing via Payments Canada Lynx or ACSS for payments to Canadian vendors; (b) cross-border SWIFT MT103 for direct electronic remittances to foreign licensors, advertising platforms, payment processors, or cloud providers; and (c) commercial letters of credit (documentary LCs) where a supplier demands bank-independent payment assurance against conforming shipping, licensing, or services documentation. A standard MT103 must include the beneficiary account/IBAN, the beneficiary bank's SWIFT BIC, and reference to the underlying software licence/support agreement in field 70 to demonstrate commercial purpose. When paying app-store intermediaries (Apple, Google) or payment aggregators, the company should reconcile the payment instruction against the platform's migration of merchant-of-record flows to avoid commingling of treasury functions. For larger commitments (monthly advertising spend exceeding CAD 500,000), a commercial LC or a standby LC may be used to increase payment certainty; the LC should be issued as an irrevocable, confirmed, at-sight letter credited to the beneficiary bank. All outbound transactions in excess of CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC record keeping; no foreign-exchange conversion pre-authorization is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR/USD currency forwards executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank or a licensed broker under the over-the-counter derivatives framework

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing CAD only for liquid offshore hedging when a physical delivery forward is operationally impractical, provided the counterparty is a regulated financial institution
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between CAD and USD or CAD and EUR, subject to standard International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) documentation

Currency options (including call and put options on CAD-USD and CAD-EUR), both OTC and exchange-traded, if the hedge relationship is properly documented under the bank's derivative licensing requirements
Interest rate and currency cross-currency basis swaps used solely for the purpose of hedging an aggregated foreign-currency cash-flow mismatch rather than for speculative trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation (or amalgamation/continuance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs CAD 100 late fee; repeated non-filing leads to administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of each fiscal year (e.g., June 30 for December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; compounded daily interest; possible criminal prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if registrant and annual filing election in effect)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than 3 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of unremitted amount plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; interest on unpaid balance; possible cancellation of registration certificate

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CBCA distributing (public) corporations must always appoint an independent auditor. Non-distributing (private) corporations may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution, provided no shareholder holding 5% or more of shares requests an audit; no revenue threshold applies for private corporations under the CBCA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public companies; for private corporations, either IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under Canadian GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under CBCA s. 21.1, the corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register at its registered office. The register must be updated within 15 days of any change in significant control, and directors must review the register at each annual meeting. The annual return to Corporations Canada requires confirmation that the ISC register has been maintained, but no separate ISC filing is submitted annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (containing Articles, By-laws, Minutes of Meetings and Resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal Part I general rate; combined federal-provincial headline rate typically 23%-31% depending on the province of deemed PE (e.g., 26.5% in Ontario, 27% in British Columbia, 23% in Alberta)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (federal rate reduced to 9% for CCPCs on first CAD 500,000 of active business income where foreign ownership is absent); SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (35% refundable for qualifying CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs) for eligible software R&D; 3-year loss carryback; 20-year non-capital loss carryforward; no special gaming tax at federal level

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via electronic EFILE / Internet File Transfer; supporting schedules include Schedule 1 (Federal Tax), Schedule 4/5 (Provincial Tax and Allocation), Schedule 7 (SBD), Schedule 25 (Loss Utilization), Schedule 88 (TP Information), and Form T106
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with self-assessed quarterly tax installments (monthly for large corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is six months after fiscal period end; balance-due is payable within two months (three months for a CCPC claiming the Small Business Deduction)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) preceded by the RP/RC program account root; mandatory identifier
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Canadian entity's BN; non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must first register with the CRA and obtain an RP account before filing the T2

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 6-digit NAICS code describing principal business activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 511210 for software and social casino game publishing; the code drives CRA industry benchmarking and TP audit risk flags

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year/month/day of fiscal year-end (must correspond to the accounting period used for financial statements)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian-resident operating subsidiary must adopt a fiscal year consistent with its audited US-GAAP/IFRS statements; non-resident payers must align the Canadian filing to the same fiscal end as the Canadian permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 300 - Sales, Revenues and Other Amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all sources, including in-app purchases (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing), advertising, and virtual goods sales, net of refunds and platform commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income for a tax-resident Canadian corporation; for a non-resident corporation, report only gross revenue attributable to the Canadian business carried on through a permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all deductions, non-capital loss carryforwards, and SBD adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute Canadian taxable income under s.115 (Canadian-source business income only); the resident treaty-protected income is excluded only if a PE is absent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1, Box 550 - Part I Aggregate Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax before foreign tax credits, calculated at 15% general rate or 9% SBD rate on eligible active business income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are not eligible for the SBD; applicable only to a Canadian-controlled private corporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income among provinces based on permanent establishment gross revenue and payroll factors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A head office in one province with a PE in another must apportion income; foreign treaty PEs outside Canada are excluded from provincial allocation only where a treaty exemption applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of carryback (3 years) and carryforward (20 years) of non-capital losses against taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian-resident entity may apply losses only against income that remains taxable in Canada; losses of a non-resident are allowed only with respect to taxable Canadian-source income and may not exceed the PE profits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 / Schedule 88 - Transfer Pricing Information Return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory information return for all reportable non-arm's length cross-border transactions with non-residents exceeding CAD 1 million
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian entity transacting with a non-resident parent (e.g., IP royalty, technology service fees, management charges) must identify the counterparty, amount, currency, pricing method, and contemporaneous documentation reference

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compound interest at prescribed rates (approx. 9%-10%) on unpaid balances; s.238/s.239 criminal prosecutions for false statements; Form T106 failures carry CAD 100-per-record penalties (min CAD 1,000, max CAD 25,000) plus a CAD 24,000 gross-negligence penalty

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer may apply a reduced treaty rate only after the beneficial owner delivers a valid Form NR301 tax declaration and the foreign competent authority's Certificate of Residence (TRC); the payer must retain the NR301/TRC, withhold at the treaty rate, remit Part XIII tax by the 15th of the month following payment, and report the payment on Form NR4; if relief documentation is unavailable, the 25% statutory rate must be withheld and the non-resident may file Form NR7-R for a refund within two years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for royalties and non-arm's length interest; arm's length interest is generally exempt; under major Canadian DTAs (e.g., Canada-US), arm's length interest is 0%, copyright/software royalties are 0%, and patent/know-how royalties are 0%, while trademark/other royalties may remain at 10%; the social casino operator's IP licenses and intercompany financing must be priced for arm's length and structured to rely on allocable treaty benefits

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is mandated when the aggregate value of reportable non-arm's length cross-border transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1 million in a fiscal year; Master File (Form RC7204) and Local File (Form RC7205) are mandated for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CAD 1 billion, with the Local File additionally conditioned on the Canadian entity's gross revenue exceeding CAD 10 million and/or reportable transactions exceeding CAD 1 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a Caribbean/Gulf-style ESR statute; instead, the CRA applies s.245 GAAR, s.247(2) transfer-pricing recharacterization, the beneficial ownership doctrine, and the OECD DEMPE functional analysis to attack substance-deficient structures. A Canadian social casino holding IP must demonstrate real employees, decision-making, IP development, enhancement, maintenance, protection, and exploitation (DEMPE) functions, and bear commensurate financial risk; otherwise revenue can be reallocated to the non-resident parent and recharacterized as a deemed dividend subject to 25% Part XIII withholding

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Licensing IP or paying platform/management fees to a non-resident parent without a written intercompany agreement, without contemporaneous comparability analysis, and without filing Form T106; backdated or circular cost allocations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% penalty on the net transfer-pricing adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 1 million or 10% of gross revenue; full reassessment and recharacterization of the adjustment as a deemed dividend or deemed interest; compound daily interest; Form T106 penalties up to CAD 25,000 plus CAD 24,000 gross-negligence penalty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false or incomplete T2/T106 returns face the 50% gross negligence penalty under s.163(2) and criminal liability under s.239(1) for knowingly making false statements; CRA may enter personal assets and impose travel bans pending criminal tax proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Part XIII / Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or deemed dividends to non-residents without withholding the statutory 25% Part XIII tax; disguising profit repatriation as management fees, intra-group loans, or cost reimbursements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full unremitted amount plus compound daily interest; late-payment penalty of 5% plus 1% per month; potential s.239 criminal prosecution with fines of 50%-200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s.227.1, directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted Part XIII and source-withholding amounts even after resignation; the CRA may pursue personal bank accounts, garnish wages, and prohibit cross-border travel without a court release

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Canadian entity with no employees, premises, or operational functions to invoice US/EU platform revenue while the actual DEMPE functions remain with the foreign parent; treaty shopping through the Canadian entity to extract dividends at reduced rates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.245 GAAR denial of the tax benefit, recharacterization of transactions, reassessment at full statutory rates, and s.163(2) gross negligence penalties of 50% of the avoided tax; denial of treaty relief for lack of beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing where the entity is a mere conduit: directors are personally assessed under s.227.1 for withholding, and knowingly signing conduit arrangements creates exposure to tax evasion prosecution and personal asset seizure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating in-app purchase revenue, fabricating expenses (fake advertising invoices, artificial content acquisition costs), destroying books, or using untraceable crypto rails to route platform payouts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.239(1), conviction on indictment: fine between 50% and 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; summary conviction: imprisonment up to 2 years less a day; the CRA + RCMP joint enforcement units routinely target gaming-adjacent digital businesses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability is imposed on signing officers; the sentencing court may issue a travel ban, restitution order, and forfeiture of proceeds; professional disqualification and reputational death are direct collateral consequences

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using simulated social casino mechanics to launder proceeds of crime through Apple IAP / Google Play Billing refunds, gift cards, or convertible virtual currency; failing to implement transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting at the corporate level
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for AML violations under the PCMLTFA; CRA and FINTRAC coordinated audits may disallow expenses funneled through unreported AML-treated flows and impose gross negligence penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly enable laundering of virtual credits face criminal money-laundering charges (Criminal Code s.462.31), imprisonment up to 10 years on indictment, travel bans, and forfeiture of personal and corporate assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying foreign directors or executives through unregistered offshore payroll without Canadian source deductions, NR4 reporting, and Part XIII withholding; providing undocumented private benefits (cryptocurrency bonuses, equity-free carried interests) to founders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unremitted source-withholding reassessments plus interest; 5% late-filing penalties; s.163(2) gross negligence penalty of 50% where the omission is made knowingly
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: s.227.1 makes each director jointly and severally liable for the entire unremitted payroll amount; personal bankruptcy does not discharge the liability; the CRA can issue a Requisition to pay and freeze personal assets
